Full Commentary:
There goes the full-time whistle! Pepe's second-half double won the game for Arsenal, lashing through the legs of Sanchez from a tight angle before finding the far corner through Dunk's legs. Everton's 5-0 defeat against Manchester City sees the Gunners leapfrog the Toffees in the table, but Tottenham's late 4-2 win over Leicester means that Spurs take seventh spot and Europa Conference League qualification. It finishes 2-0 to Arsenal at the Emirates!
--- 90’ +2 Full time FULL-TIME: ARSENAL 2-0 BRIGHTON AND HOVE ALBION ---
(90’) Tottenham have come from behind at the King Power Stadium and now are now 3-2 up against Leicester City. If things stay as they are, Spurs will finish seventh and earn Europa Conference League qualification, with Arsenal ending the season in eighth.
(88’) Saka has moved into a central role behind Lacazette now, with substitute Martinelli going out to the left wing.
--- 86’ Substitution Arteta replaces Odegaard now, and the on-loan attacking midfielder is received warmly by the Arsenal supporters as Martinelli takes his place. Gabriel Martinelli Martin Ødegaard ---
(83’) Odegaard presses with tenacity, chasing the ball down all the way into the Brighton third and out to the left, where Saka looks to nick the ball, but Dunk goes down and the referee's whistle bails him out. The Arsenal players feel he went down too easily, but the free-kick is given nonetheless.
(81’) Arsenal are just slowing the pace of the game down now and look in complete control of proceedings, working the ball around confidently.
--- 79’ Substitution Arteta makes another change now, with Aubameyang replaced up front by Lacazette in what could be the Frenchman's final game for Arsenal. Alexandre Lacazette Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang ---
(76’) Pepe, on a hat-trick, is being afforded a little more freedom in attack now, with Odegaard drifting out to the right to cover for the Ivorian when the Gunners don't have the ball, while Pepe pushes up and presses alongside Aubameyang in the centre.
--- 74’ Substitution Arteta makes his first change of the afternoon, replacing Smith Rowe with fellow academy product Saka on the left for the remainder of the game. Bukayo Saka Emile Smith-Rowe ---
--- 73’ Highlight CROSSBAR! Gabriel threads a pass into the feet of Partey on the edge of the box with his back to goal and the midfielder pops the ball into the air as he swivels and thumps a volley at goal, but it cannons back off the crossbar! He was inches away from his first Arsenal goal there! ---
(71’) Arsenal are in a confident mood now and are playing with freedom and confidence. Aubameyang cleverly dummies a pass, allowing it to run for Smith Rowe, but the attacking midfielder's cut-back is blocked.
(69’) Some quick, sharp passing through the centre sees Aubameyang release Pepe, who tries to chip the goalkeeper but gets his execution all wrong and the ball simply bounces through for Sanchez to gather.
--- 68’ Highlight WIDE! Aubameyang is released down the left by Smith Rowe and sprints away from Webster, but he snatches at his effort with his left foot and slices wide of the near post! ---
--- 66’ Substitution Potter makes a third change now as he looks to get his side back on level terms, bringing Mac Allister off for Alzate. Steven Alzate Alexis Mac Allister ---
--- 64’ Highlight SAVE! Moder drives into space on the left and tries to catch Leno out with a powerful drive from range, but the Arsenal keeper flings himself to his right and palms the shot away! ---
(62’) This is the first season that Arsenal have had three players score at least 10 Premier League goals (Lacazette, Aubameyang, Pepe) since 2016/17 (Alexis Sanchez, Olivier Giroud, Theo Walcott).
--- 60’ Assist Odegaard's pass into the right channel for Pepe was weighted and placed perfectly for Pepe to take it on his left and drift inside before picking out the far corner. Martin Ødegaard ---
--- 60’ Goal! GOAL!!! PEPE DOUBLES ARSENAL'S LEAD!!! Odegaard slips it in behind for Pepe down the right and the winger drives into the box before slotting his strike through Dunk's legs and into the bottom-left corner! It's 2-0 to Arsenal! Nicolas Pépé 0.05 xG 0.40 xGOT ---
--- 57’ Highlight WIDE! Brighton are committing more bodies forward now and Bissouma goes for the bottom-left corner from the edge of the box, but he arrows his low strike just the wrong side of the post! ---
(55’) No player has been involved in more goals in all competitions for Arsenal this season than Pepe (15 goals and five assists).
--- 53’ Highlight NO PENALTY! Aubameyang is played through down the left and he surges into the box before cutting onto his right and sliding the ball across to Odegaard, arriving in the middle. The midfielder goes down under pressure from Lallana, but the referee ignores the Gunners' furious appeals and does not award a penalty! ---
--- 51’ Highlight MISS! Just moments after scoring, Arsenal nearly concede as Connolly picks the ball up in the Arsenal box and curls towards the far corner, but he gets it all wrong and fires wide! He had to hit the target from there! ---
--- 49’ Assist Chambers' low cross has loads of pace on it and was difficult for Pepe to take in, but the Ivorian controlled well, making a yard for himself before drilling into the net! Calum Chambers ---
--- 49’ Goal! GOAL!!! ARSENAL ARE IN FRONT!! Chambers is found on the right and fizzes a low cross into the box that Pepe does well to control, popping it up into the air before lashing through the legs of Sanchez from a tight angle with his weaker right foot! It's 1-0 to Arsenal! Nicolas Pépé 0.06 xG 0.09 xGOT ---
(47’) Gabriel dallies on the ball for a moment too long before trying to pick Aubameyang out over the top and the striker ends up being caught offside.
(46’) We're back underway for the second half!
--- 46’ Substitution Jahanbakhsh is the second Brighton player to be replaced at the break, with Lallana replacing him and allowing Mac Allister to move into a more advanced role. Adam Lallana Alireza Jahanbakhsh ---
--- 46’ Substitution Potter makes two half-time changes as he looks for an improved showing from his side in the second half. Trossard is the first to make way, being replaced in attack by the hard-working Connolly. Aaron Connolly Leandro Trossard ---
Arsenal have enjoyed almost 62% of the ball and have taken 11 shots to Brighton's two, but the Gunners have registered just three shots on target. The hosts have been the better side, but they need to do more to breach the Brighton defence and capitalise on the opportunity to rise to seventh.
There goes the half-time whistle! Arsenal have been on top but have failed to convert their dominance into a lead to this point. Gabriel hit the bar with a deflected header just before the break and Holding prodded just over the line from a corner, but the offside flag denied him. Brighton have offered little going forward, but have congested the centre of the pitch and made it difficult for the Gunners to pick them apart. It's 0-0 at the break!
--- 45’ Half time HALF-TIME: ARSENAL 0-0 BRIGHTON AND HOVE ALBION ---
--- 43’ Highlight CROSSBAR! Gabriel, who had stayed in the box following a corner, is picked out at the back post with a lofted pass in from deep and the Arsenal defender's header loops goalwards off the head of Dunk, but it clips the bar and goes behind! ---
(41’) Results elsewhere are still in Arsenal's favour but the Gunners still haven't been able to get themselves ahead. They've created a number of half-chances, but are yet to really carve Brighton open.
--- 39’ Highlight CHANCE! Pepe controls the ball on the right beautifully and drives threateningly into the box before cutting the ball back to Odegaard, whose cross towards Aubameyang at the back post is spilled by Sanchez, but the goalkeeper smothers the loose ball! ---
(37’) Brighton are not at all pleased that Holding escapes without a booking as the defender hauls Moder down on the touchline during a Seagulls attack. A free-kick is all that's given, however.
--- 35’ Highlight BLOCK! Brighton do pull the trigger now as Moder runs onto the ball on the edge of the Arsenal box and hits it first-time, but his effort is blocked away and Dunk hits a very ambitious follow-up well over the top from some distance out. ---
(33’) Burn tries to pick Trossard out in behind, but the flag goes up for offside. The visitors are yet to have a shot of any kind and seem to be struggling to create chances.
--- 31’ Highlight NO GOAL! Odegaard whips in a terrific corner from the right that Partey flicks on to Holding just a few yards out. The defender controls and prods at goal, but White is there to clear it off the line! Replays suggest that the ball had just crept in, but the flag goes up against Holding and it won't count! ---
(29’) Smith Rowe is fouled in a dangerous position 20 yards from goal and Xhaka steps up to strike the free-kick, but he thumps it straight into the wall and it squirms into the arms of Sanchez. That was a disappointing effort.
--- 27’ Highlight SAVE! Arsenal counter themselves after Tierney's outstanding piece of defending and Partey goes for goal from the edge of the box, lashing a vicious effort just under the crossbar, but Sanchez stays tall and tips it over! ---
--- 26’ Highlight GREAT DEFENDING! Arsenal lose the ball after a poorly-worked free-kick and Brighton break quickly, with Tierney left on his own to defend a two-on-one. The left-back positions himself superbly to prevent the square ball before closing down at the last moment to block Jahanbaksh's attempt and it bounces into the grateful grasp of Leno! ---
--- 24’ Highlight WIDE! Tierney wins the ball off White right on the Brighton byline and sends it back towards Aubameyang, who switches it out to Odegaard on the right before darting to the back post to meet the Norwegian's cross, but he can only nod wide under pressure from Webster! ---
(22’) Neither side has managed to create anything of note in the last few minutes. It's been very back-and-forth with little goalmouth action.
(20’) Elsewhere, Jamie Vardy has put Leicester City ahead against Tottenham, while Everton are 2-0 down against Manchester City. As things stand, an Arsenal win would lift the Gunners into seventh and secure them Europa Conference League qualification. There's plenty of time for things to change, of course.
(18’) Arsenal pepper the Brighton box with crosses, including an excellent delivery from Chambers on the right, but Brighton defend capably and weather the storm.
(16’) Arsenal have pushed forward and the whole Brighton team is camped back in their half as the Gunners probe for an opening. It's very congested in the centre, however, and there's not much space for the hosts to exploit.
(14’) Bissouma picks out a long ball over the top to Jahanbakhsh, making a run in behind, but it's a fraction ahead of the forward and Leno is out to smother the chance.
(12’) An incisive Arsenal counter sees Smith Rowe slide the ball down the left for Tierney, who whips in a superb cross, but nobody is in the box to attack it!
(10’) Smith Rowe leads an Arsenal counter down the left as Brighton are caught very high up the field. He gallops towards the corner before laying it back to Odegaard, but the midfielder lashes over via a nick off White!
(8’) Pepe cuts in from the right and decides to have a shot of his own from distance, but it clatters back out off a defender. The box is packed with bodies and there's no clear way through.
--- 7’ Highlight SHOTS! Partey receives the ball on the edge of the box before taking a touch to set himself, but he curls just wide of the far corner. Just moments later, his midfield partner Xhaka also lets fly from range, but Sanchez gets to it and keeps it out! ---
(5’) Arsenal force a corner as Smith Rowe makes a sharp run down the left after some clever interchanges, but Webster slides in to block the cut-back behind for a corner.
(3’) Brighton appear to be playing in a narrow 4-3-1-2 today. White and Burn start as full-backs, while Mac Allister plays in the space between the midfield three and the front two of Trossard and Jahanbakhsh.
(1’) We're underway at the Emirates for the last time this season!
Meanwhile, Brighton have won their final league game in just one of the last six campaigns (D3 L2), though that victory did come last season as they beat Burnley 2-1 at Turf Moor.
Arsenal haven’t lost their final league game of the season since 2004/05, and have won each of their last nine games to end a Premier League campaign. In fact, when finishing a Premier League season at home, Arsenal have won each of their last 11 matches.
Brighton boss Graham Potter, meanwhile, makes two changes of his own following his team's shock 3-2 win over champions Manchester City. Dunk and Trossard come into the side, with Alzate dropping to the bench and the injured Danny Welbeck missing out entirely. The former Arsenal striker joins Solly March, Joel Veltman, Davy Propper and Tariq Lamptey on the treatment table, while Neal Maupay is suspended.
Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta makes two changes to the side that battled to a late 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace last time out. Saka and Elneny drop to the bench, with Odegaard and Xhaka coming into the starting line-up. David Luiz and Hector Bellerin are out injured, with the former confirmed to be leaving upon the expiry of his contract this summer, while on-loan goalkeeper Mat Ryan is ineligible to face his parent club and may also have played his last game for Arsenal unless the club seek to make his stay permanent.
Brighton and Hove Albion substitutes: Andi Zeqiri, Michal Karbownik, Thomas McGill, Adam Lallana, Percy Tau, Aaron Connolly, Jason Steele, Steven Alzate, Moises Caicedo.
Brighton and Hove Albion XI (4-3-1-2): Robert Sanchez; Ben White, Adam Webster, Lewis Dunk, Dan Burn; Pascal Gross, Yves Bissouma, Jakub Moder; Alexis Mac Allister; Alireza Jahanbakhsh, Leandro Trossard.
Arsenal substitutes: Cedric Soares, Alexandre Lacazette, Pablo Mari, Runar Alex Runarsson, Mohamed Elneny, Dani Ceballos, Eddie Nketiah, Bukayo Saka, Gabriel Martinelli.
Arsenal XI (4-2-3-1): Bernd Leno; Calum Chambers, Rob Holding, Gabriel Magalhaes, Kieran Tierney; Thomas Partey, Granit Xhaka; Nicolas Pepe, Martin Odegaard, Emile Smith Rowe; Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang.
Ninth-placed Arsenal could end the season in seventh if they beat Brighton this afternoon and both Everton and Tottenham fail to secure victory - a set of results which would see the Gunners qualify for the inaugural Europa Conference League. Brighton, meanwhile, are assured of safety and can play without pressure.
Hello and welcome to our LIVE coverage of the clash between Arsenal and Brighton and Hove Albion at the Emirates Stadium on the final day of the 2020/21 Premier League season.

That's all for today. Until next time, goodbye!
One more huge game to come for Chelsea, who face Manchester City in the Champions League final next week. As for Villa, having narrowly avoided relegation last term, they can celebrate a season of significant progress as they comfortably finish mid-table.
Despite defeat at Villa Park, Chelsea secured Champions League football next season. Villa, who finish 11th, sign off an impressive season in style thanks to goals from Bertrand Traore and Anwar El Ghazi. Although Ben Chilwell pulled one back for the Blues, they were unable to find an equaliser. Nevertheless, following Leicester's defeat by Tottenham, their overall mission is accomplished.
--- 90’ +6 Full time FULL-TIME: ASTON VILLA 2-1 CHELSEA ---
--- 90’ +5 Yellow card Kepa is booked in the dying moments. Kepa Arrizabalaga ---
(90’) Whatever happens here, Chelsea are all but certain to secure Champions League football for next season. Tottenham have made it 4-2 against Leicester, who will have to settle for a fifth-place finish.
(90’) We are going to have five additional minutes at the end of this game.
--- 89’ Red card! RED CARD FOR AZPILICUETA! Chelsea down to 10 men! The Blues skipper is given his marching orders as he reacts to Grealish's foul by pushing his hand into the face of the Villa talisman. Contact was minimal and Grealish certainly made the most of it, but that was irresponsible from the Spaniard. César Azpilicueta ---
--- 87’ Highlight Great save! Martinez to the rescue for Villa - as has so often been the case this season. The goalkeeper gets across his line quickly to deny Chilwell, who looked to turn home from Ziyech's cross. ---
(85’) Chilwell has visions of Marco van Basten as he looks to volley home from Silva's diagonal ball. Of course, the former Dutch striker executed one of the most iconic volleys in football history during the 1988 European Championship final. But the England left-back is not so successful 33 years on, slicing his attempt well wide.
(83’) Tottenham lead at Leicester! Spurs are now 3-2 to the good against the Foxes. That consolidates Chelsea's place in the top four for now. The Blues will not want to rely on results elsewhere, though.
--- 81’ Yellow card Martinez is deemed to have kicked the ball away as Chelsea wait to take a corner, and is booked. Emiliano Martinez ---
--- 79’ Substitution El Ghazi is given a well-earned rest by Smith, who introduces Jacob Ramsey in his place. Jacob Ramsey Anwar El-Ghazi ---
(77’) Azpilicueta goes for goal with a powerful strike from the edge of the box. But it is high and wide of the target.
--- 76’ Highlight Good block! Chelsea looking to level and the ball falls nicely for Havertz in the box. The German volleys towards goal, but his effort is blocked by the well-placed Mings. ---
(75’) Tottenham have equalised again at Leicester, while Liverpool are now 2-0 up against Crystal Palace. That means Chelsea return to the top four heading into the final 15 minutes of the season.
--- 74’ Yellow card Nakamba has his name taken by the referee for time-wasting. Marvelous Nakamba ---
--- 73’ Substitution Traore given a rest by Villa as he goes off to be replaced by youngster Carney Chukwuemeka. Carney Chukwuemeka Bertrand Traoré ---
--- 70’ Assist Pulisic's inviting cross after the one-two with Ziyech was simply begging to be attacked. Chilwell duly obliged. Game on! Christian Pulisic ---
--- 70’ Goal! CHILWELL!!! 2-1! Hope for Chelsea! Following a lovely move down the right side, Pulisic plays a neat one-two with Ziyech before crossing. Although Werner does not connect, Chilwell arrives late at the far post and his volley is over the line before Martinez claws it out. Ben Chilwell 0.45 xG 0.43 xGOT ---
--- 68’ Highlight Chance! Almost an immediate impact by Havertz. The German arrives late to meet Chilwell's deep cross to the far post. But under pressure from Targett, he is unable to keep his volley down. ---
--- 66’ Substitution Kai Havertz is introduced by Chelsea with Kovacic making way. Kai Havertz Mateo Kovacic ---
--- 65’ Yellow card McGinn catches Silva late and goes into the book. John McGinn ---
(64’) James' poor pass is intercepted by Watkins, who looks to race in behind the Chelsea defence. Thankfully for the visitors, Rudiger is there to tidy up the danger.
(62’) It has been a frustrating day for Chelsea so far. Their latest attack culminates in the ball dropping for Kovacic, who blazes his volley wildly high.
--- 60’ Substitution Another Chelsea change with Hakim Ziyech replacing Jorginho. Hakim Ziyech Jorginho ---
--- 59’ Highlight OFFSIDE! NO GOAL! A lovely move by Chelsea culminates in Mount sliding the ball through for Azpilicueta. The skipper is intercepted but it breaks for Werner, who finishes. However, his joy is short-lived as the offside flag is raised against Azpilicueta. ---
(57’) Villa go in search of a third and Grealish looks to play a one-two with El Ghazi in the box. However, the attempted return pass is lacking the required execution and Chelsea clear.
(55’) The visitors look to respond and Mount works space to shoot from the edge of the box. There is plenty of power in his effort, but it flies just wide of the post with Martinez flat-footed.
(54’) To compound Chelsea's misery, Leicester have not long retaken the lead against Tottenham thanks to another Jamie Vardy penalty. As things stand, the Blues slip to fifth place once more.
--- 52’ Goal! EL GHAZI!!! 2-0 VILLA! Breathing space for the hosts as El Ghazi steps up and calmly sends Kepa the wrong way. Anwar El-Ghazi 0.79 xG 0.95 xGOT ---
--- 51’ Highlight PENALTY TO VILLA! Following a good spell of pressure by the hosts, Jorginho trips Traore in the box and the referee points straight to the spot. ---
--- 49’ Yellow card Kovacic is booked for taking out Grealish, who was threatening to counter for Villa. Mateo Kovacic ---
(47’) A good break from Chelsea! Kovacic leads the charge for the Blues, who get away down the left flank. Werner eventually cuts the ball back for Pulisic, whose scuffed strike deflects off Targett before spinning narrowly wide of the target.
(46’) Villa get the ball rolling again in the second half.
--- 46’ Substitution Chelsea make a change in goal at the break with Kepa Arrizabalaga replacing Mendy, who injured himself while attempting to save Villa's first goal. Kepa Arrizabalaga Edouard Mendy ---
Just to remind you of the current state of play. Following Tottenham's equaliser against Leicester, Chelsea occupy fourth place and are above the Foxes on goal difference. Liverpool, who lead Crystal Palace, are now third, but the Blues' fate is very much in their own hands.
Despite dominating most of the first half, Chelsea trail in a game they must win to guarantee Champions League football next season. Ironically, Bertrand Traore - a former Blue - was the man who gave Villa the lead just before half-time. The visitors have had plenty of chances to get their noses in front, and will hope they are not made to rue them.
--- 45’ +3 Half time HALF-TIME: ASTON VILLA 1-0 CHELSEA ---
--- 45’ +2 Yellow card Werner has his name taken for a foul on Traore. Chelsea's frustrations are in danger of boiling over here. Timo Werner ---
--- 45’ Yellow card Jorginho blocks off the run of El Ghazi and goes into the book. Jorginho ---
--- 43’ Assist Targett demonstrated brilliant awareness to pick out Traore, who lost his marker too easily in the box. Matt Targett ---
--- 43’ Goal! TRAORE!!! 1-0 VILLA! The hosts lead against the run of play! The former Chelsea man is unmarked as he meets Targett's low corner into the box. Although he scuffs his first-time shot into the ground, it loops over the dive of Mendy and goes in off the crossbar. Bertrand Traoré 0.06 xG 0.30 xGOT ---
(42’) Tuchel said in the lead-up to this game that he would pay no attention to the other ongoing games during the first half here. He knows his side must focus purely on getting the job done themselves.
(40’) Tottenham have equalised at the King Power Stadium. Harry Kane's goal brings them level against Leicester, who drop back out of the top four. As a result, Chelsea are back in the Champions League spots.
(38’) Villa look to pose a threat with a succession of free-kicks into the box. But Chelsea deal with the delivery on both occasions.
(36’) Liverpool lead at Crystal Palace thanks to Sadio Mane's strike. With Leicester also in front against Tottenham, Chelsea drop out of the top four for the time being.
(34’) For all their possession, it is important that Chelsea take their chances. They will be desperate not to rue those missed chances earlier on.
(32’) A rare threat from Villa, but Chelsea have certainly been the stronger of the two sides so far. In fact, the Blues have enjoyed a whopping 70 per cent of the possession.
(29’) Not far away! In almost identical fashion, McGinn has an opportunity for the hosts within 60 seconds of Traore. Once again, the Scotsman looks for the far corner with a left-footed strike, but Mendy sees it wide.
(28’) The noise levels at Villa Park rise as the hosts embark on a rare venture forward. Space opens for Traore to try his luck from distance, and his bending effort is not too far wide of the post.
(26’) Villa riding their luck at the moment, although they have avoided defeat against Chelsea on all four previous occasions that they have locked horns on the final day of a Premier League season.
--- 24’ Highlight What a chance! Azpilicueta neatly cushions Pulisic's diagonal ball into the path of the onrushing Mount. But the England international sends his volley high into the stand. ---
(22’) The Blues threaten still. Once again, Villa cannot clear and Pulisic attempts a spectacular overhead kick. Unfortunately, the American international does not connect cleanly and Martinez gathers.
(20’) Mount also faced Villa during his loan spell with Derby County in the 2018-19 season. The midfielder was part of the Rams side that were beaten 2-1 by Dean Smith's side in the Championship play-off final at Wembley.
(18’) Chelsea continue to apply the pressure. Another set-piece culminates in Werner teeing the ball up for Mount to unleash a clean strike that Martinez does well to hold onto.
(17’) Elsewhere, Leicester have just taken the lead against Tottenham thanks to a Jamie Vardy penalty. That pushes Chelsea down to fourth place as things stand, so they will want to get their noses in front as soon as possible here.
(15’) A Chelsea corner is not properly cleared by Villa and the ball breaks kindly for Chilwell to strike. The left-back's volley is on target, but straight into the arms of Martinez.
(13’) The Blues have won on each of their last three Premier League visits to Villa, and they will be encouraged by the start they have made here.
--- 11’ Highlight Werner should do better! Azpilicueta does well to control a diagonal ball into the box and keep the move alive by sending it into the box. Werner attacks the delivery, but cannot direct the ball towards goal. ---
(9’) Another opportunity for Mount following a good move by the visitors. However, his attempted shot is charged down by Nakamba.
(7’) Currently third, Chelsea are in pole position for a Champions League place. But the Blues will not be taking anything for granted, as they can still be overtaken by Leicester and Liverpool.
(5’) The referee wants a word with Grealish, who unnecessarily ran into the back of Jorginho while chasing a loose ball. The Villa skipper gets a stern telling for his troubles.
(3’) A long ball into the Villa box is only cleared as far as Mount, but he sends his volley well wide of the target.
(1’) The referee blows his whistle and Chelsea get the match underway.
The players receive a warm welcome from the returning supporters at Villa Park and kick-off is moments away.
Chelsea have only lost their final Premier League game once in the last nine seasons. Should they continue their impressive record here, the Blues will be playing Champions League football next season.

Dean Smith names an unchanged side from Villa's midweek win at Tottenham. Emiliano Martinez and Matt Targett have now started every game this season, while Marvelous Nakamba makes his 50th appearance for the club.

All the onus is on Chelsea on the final day of the Premier League season. The Blues will secure a place in next season's Champions League with three points against Villa, who are guaranteed an 11th-placed finish whatever happens today.

The result means that Newcastle climb up to 12th to end the season. Meanwhile, Fulham finish 18th.
Willock and Schar ensure that Newcastle collect a 2-0 win - and that Fulham fall to another defeat. The hosts started brightly: Cavaleiro and Lookman both came close to opening the scoring and it looked like the beginning of a promising display. However, Newcastle took the lead on the counter when Willock surged into the Fulham box before sweeping beyond Rodak, for his seventh goal in seven consecutive games. The hosts fought hard for an equaliser and their closest moment came in the second half when Cavaleiro missed a one-on-one. In a familiar story for the relegated side though, they failed to capitalise on their opportunities, and when Ritchie won a late penalty, Schar stepped up to punish Fulham and make it 2-0,

(90’) Well, it's looking like another defeat for Fulham. They've played well in the second half, but just couldn't quite score - and now they've been punished by Schar's penalty.

(76’) Zaha gets into the area on the left and skips away from Godfrey, but his attempted low cross is blocked.

(73’) Coleman comes infield from the right and unleashes his inner Quaresma with a gratuitous outside-of-the-boot pass, looking to spin it out to Digne on the left. It's blocked at the edge of the area but almost drops to Sigurdsson, who can't quite hook his boot back to tee himself up for a shot.
(72’) Less than 20 minutes of the 90 to play now. Palace have been much improved since Rodriguez scored but their final ball has been lacking so far. You would think a second Everton goal now might kill it.
(70’) A corner on the left is taken short to Zaha and he teases in a cross towards the far post. Benteke attacks it but can't quite get a touch and it fades behind for a goal kick.

--- 68’ Substitution Palace make their first change, with Schlupp coming on to replace Riedewald. Jeffrey Schlupp Jairo Riedewald ---
(67’) Rodriguez gives Digne a ball to chase down the left channel, and the left-back harries Ward all the way to the byline to try and get to it. Ward and Kouyate have to combine to get it clear but the flag eventually goes up.
(65’) Ayew comes infield from the right and has a pop from range, but it's a simple enough save for Olsen down to his left. Palace have come to life in the last few minutes.
(64’) Zaha intercepts a pass from Davies just inside the Everton half and drives into the area, jinking away from Keane at the edge of the box to get the ball onto his left foot for a shot. Eventually, he's just forced wide enough that the best he can do is hit it straight at Olsen.

(50’) Eze goes down in the area under a challenge from Holgate. He wants a penalty and has a word with the ref after the incident, but it was a good tackle and a good decision.
(49’) Benteke holds the ball up at the edge of the area with Ayew and Zaha in support. He opts to find the former but the Everton back line stands firm and the attackers can't pick a way through.

(45’) We're back underway.
With Mateta, Batshuayi and Townsend, the Palace bench perhaps has a few more attacking options than Everton's tonight. Everton's does contain Gbamin for the first time since August 2019, and Ancelotti said before the game that he's looking to get him on at some point.
A game that has threatened to burst into life without ever properly getting going, though Everton will feel they should be ahead. Richarlison in particular has had a few chances to break the deadlock but both he and Calvert-Lewin have been thwarted by Guaita. The home side can be satisfied with their performance so far but Palace have looked threatening when Zaha and Eze have managed to find pockets of space to run into.

(35’) Digne checks onto his right foot and bends an inswinging cross towards Calvert-Lewin on the penalty spot, but a Palace defender gets across to head clear.
(34’) Benteke lays off Van Aanholt with a lovely flicked pass at the edge of the area but the left-back can't take it cleanly as he bursts infield and the ball goes astray.

(26’) Zaha works the ball onto his left foot around 25 yards out, but drags a low shot across goal and wide to the right of goal.
(25’) The game has really livened up after a slow start. Everton will be annoyed not to be ahead, after two very presentable chances for Richarlison and Calvert-Lewin.

Nine-man Newcastle cling onto a priceless win over Southampton. This was a thrilling, end-to-end game throughout and Newcastle quickly took advantage to secure a commanding early lead. Manchester City go four points clear at the top of the Premier League table with a narrow win over Sheffield United courtesy of Jesus' close-range goal inside the first nine minutes after fine work from Torres. The Blades hung on and came close to an equaliser late on as Fleck fired a half-volley just wide, but City's dominance in possession helped them claim all three points. It finishes 1-0 to City!

(76’) Foden drives down the left and fires a low ball into the middle, but it's blocked behind for a corner by Egan.
(74’) Wilder appears to be readying a couple of substitutions on the Sheffield United bench. His side have stayed in the game and perhaps they can stun the hosts with some changes.

City put together a lovely, flowing move as Silva surges down the right before exchanging passes with Gundogan and switching to Foden, who lays it off for Zinchenko to run onto just outside the box. The left-back smacks an effort across goal, but Ramsdale gets across to palm the stinging drive around the post! ---
(69’) City are still patiently working the ball around as they search for openings, but Sheffield United remain stubbornly organised in their low block and refuse to be carved open.
--- 67’ Highlight NO PENALTY! Torres is released in behind and he speeds away from Bogle before going down in the box as the Sheffield United defender puts an arm into his back, but the referee shakes his head and points for a goal-kick! ---

--- 62’ Substitution Wilder makes his first change of the game, bringing Brewster - who has hardly touched the ball - off for McGoldrick up front. David McGoldrick Rhian Brewster ---
--- 60’ Highlight OVER! Sheffield United have a rare chance as a right-wing cross is headed only half-clear to the left side of the box, where Bogle arrives unmarked, but the full-back lashes high over the bar! What a waste. ---

--- 56’ Highlight SAVE! Jesus races onto a lofted ball in the box and diverts it at goal on the volley, but Ramsdale is quick off his line and makes a brave stop! ---
(54’) City haven't lost a home Premier League game when leading at half-time since April 2018 against Manchester United. Guardiola will expect his men to keep that run going with an efficient, professional second-half performance.
(52’) Lundstram and Foden collide as they compete for the ball and both players are down and require medical attention. Foden requires more extensive treatment but both are eventually okay and are able to continue.

There goes the half-time whistle! City lead at the interval courtesy of a Jesus strike from close range after superb individual work from Torres down the right. (22’) Sheffield United have seen less than 25% of the ball so far and are having to do an awful lot of chasing. They can't seem to keep possession even when they have it, often lumping it hopefully forward and straight back to the hosts.
(20’) Fernandinho dinks a superb ball over the top for Jesus to run onto, but he's tracked all the way and eventually dispossessed.

The teams have emerged at Selhurst Park and we'll just be moments away from kicking off.
It's seven years since these two sides last met in the Championship, when they played out a 2-2 draw thanks to doubles from Glenn Murray and Steve Morrison. But their last Premier League meeting requires a much further dive into history, all the way back to January 1998. Leeds ran out comfortable 2-0 victors that day away from home, thanks to goals from Rodney Wallace and Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink - while Erling Haaland's father Alfe-Inge came off the bench for the Whites.
The absence of Pablo Hernandez for Leeds is a noticeable one. The veteran Spaniard is a noted, passionate individual, and since his rather innocuous arrival at the club, has emerged as one of the players at the heart of the Bielsa revolution. But at 35, he is into the twilight of his career - and having played just a full game only once since football was suspended for a British lockdown in March, it's easy to wonder if he is slowly being phased out. (His reaction to be substituted in defeat to Leicester last time out was striking.)
It's something of a testament to the weight that Palace have in their squad now that they can choose to leave players like Christian Benteke and Michy Batshuayi - current Belgium internationals - on the bench, as extra firepower. That being said, Leeds have quite the talent of their own in reserve; former Sporting and Rennes man Raphinha may be young but has looked the business on his cameos so far this season.
